Multi-hop neighbor sampling

Source: R/graph-sampling.R
sample_neighbors.Rd

Samples the computation graph of a set of seed nodes, as in GraphSAGE (Hamilton et al. 2017) and PyG's NeighborLoader. Hop k samples up to fanouts[k] incoming edges of every node reached in hop k - 1 (hop 0 is the seed set); sources of the sampled edges join the subgraph. Messages in a GNN flow along these edges towards the seeds, so an L layer model with L fanouts sees exactly the information it would see on the full graph when every fanout is -1 (all neighbors).

Usage

sample_neighbors(g, seeds, fanouts, replace = FALSE, seed = NULL)

Arguments

g

A graph_data object.

seeds

Integer vector of seed node indices (one based).

fanouts

Integer vector, one entry per hop; -1 keeps all incoming edges.

replace

Sample edges with replacement.

seed

Optional integer seed.

Value

A graph_data object of class sampled_graph.

Details

The result is a graph_data object with local indices and these extra fields:

  • n_id: original index of every local node; the seeds come first, in the order given, so seed_index = seq_along(seeds);

  • e_id: original stored edge index of every sampled edge;

  • hop: hop at which each node was first reached (0 for seeds);

  • num_seeds.

Losses and metrics must use only the seed rows (seed_index); the other nodes are context. train_graph_model() does this automatically. The sampled graph is marked directed because sampling may keep only one direction of an undirected pair.

Sampling uses R's random number generator. With seed, it runs inside withr::with_seed(), so the result is reproducible and the caller's random state is left untouched.

Examples

g <- dataset_karate()
sg <- sample_neighbors(g, seeds = c(1, 34), fanouts = c(3, 2), seed = 1)
sg$num_seeds
#> [1] 2
sg$n_id
#>  [1]  1 34  6 12 14 19 21 27 11  2  4 33 30
